messages:
maria_g: FYI we just got a DSAR for user alice@example.com. The tricky part: embeddings for that user were copied during a tenant migration and exist in two different org buckets and a backup snapshot. Need a safe rollback + deletion procedure that preserves auditability. Any quick guidance?

ajay: Do we have the embedding IDs? If we can enumerate IDs we can coordinate deletes in vectordb + invalidate caches. Also need to check whether those backups are encrypted under customer KMS or our global key.

phil_k: If backups were taken with the same KMS key as current storage, deleting the object + KMS rotation won't be sufficient for a legal deletion — we need to delete all copies and record the delete ops. For cross-account copies we should trigger the cross-account delete API.

elena_s: Quick checklist: 1) enumerate all locations (s3, backup-snapshots, vectordb replicas) 2) snapshot evidence (hashes) before deletion 3) run deletes via admin-delete endpoint 4) append audit events to retention-exceptions log 5) notify legal for hold/exception.

maria_g: Thanks. I have partial list: s3://redwood-embeddings-prod/2024/07/migrated/sha256-abc123, vectordb cluster rr-east-2 replica-01, and a glacier snapshot gl-20240701-44. The embeddings are keyed by user_id so we can query. Who can run the admin-delete in prod?

ajay: @phil_k or @elena_s can run, but we should create a short-lived RBAC token scoped to delete-job:dsar-2112345678. Preferably use an ephemeral admin role so we don't touch our long-lived keys.

phil_k: I'll create the job. Steps I'm planning: 
- create ephemeral role via idp: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/dsar-ephemeral --duration-seconds 3600`
- run deletion script: ```bash
# list embeddings
psql -h shadowsql -U admin -c "select id from embeddings where user_id='alice@example.com';"
# delete from vectordb
curl -X POST https://internal-api/vectordb/admin/delete -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL_TOKEN" -d '{"ids": ["sha256-abc123"]}'
# delete s3 objects
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-embeddings-prod/2024/07/migrated/sha256-abc123 --region us-east-1
```
I'll capture stdout/stderr into the incident artifact bucket.

elena_s: Note on KMS: if the Glacier snapshot used a different CMK owned by another account, file a cross-account delete request with infra and add the request ID to audit. If infra can't delete (legal hold), we may need an approved retention-exception and coordinate with legal.

maria_g: One more question — what about embeddings cached in running inference nodes (KV cache)? We should invalidate caches to avoid serving stale content.

ajay: We'll push a cache-invalidate event to the routing tier. Suggest a short TTL flush and per-model key eviction for any model that has references to the user ids. I'll create the route: `POST /admin/cache/invalidate {"scope": "embeddings", "keys": ["sha256-abc123"]}`

phil_k: After deletes, append a signed audit entry: `audit-log append --case dsar-2112345678 --actor phil_k --action deletions --objects sha256-abc123 --evidence s3://redwood-artifacts/dsar-2112345678/`

elena_s: Also add a KMS key rotation marker if we rotate the CMK after deletion — but document that rotation is NOT a substitute for deletion. Include proof-of-delete hashes in the DSAR evidence bundle.

maria_g: Perfect. I'll coordinate with legal on hold/exception and open an infra ticket for cross-account Glacier deletion if needed. Phil, please run the ephemeral job when ready and ping here with the artifact links.

sec-bot: Incident artifact created: s3://redwood-artifacts/dsar-2112345678/ (contains pre-delete hashes). Policy reminder: DSAR workflow v2.3 requires audit entries for each storage layer.

phil_k: Job kicked off at 2112350800. Deleted from vectordb replica-01; S3 object removed; queued glacier cross-account delete request (req-7890). Logs: s3://redwood-artifacts/dsar-2112345678/run-20240701.log

maria_g: Thanks team. Leaving this open until legal confirms no hold. If they approve deletion we can close; otherwise we mark retention-exception and document why.

ajay: Adding a follow-up: we should add a quick automated reconciliation that runs for 7 days to verify deletes propagated to all replicas, then auto-archive the audit bundle. I'll spin up a short cron job: `DELETE_RECON_JOB=dsar-2112345678-recon`

elena_s: Filed a legal notification ticket: legal#4532. Marking thread for postmortem if cross-account deletions take >72h.

maria_g: Noted — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
